name: Heathrow Terminal 5
description: Terminal 5 at London Heathrow, where the trip started with breakfast before the short flight north to Edinburgh.

name: Edinburgh Airport
description: Scotland's busiest airport, on the western edge of Edinburgh. These photos were taken from the road heading north from the airport toward the Forth crossings.

name: M90 near Kinross
description: The M90 motorway passes Kinross and Loch Leven on the way from the Forth bridges into Fife and Perthshire.

name: Howe of Fife
description: The Howe of Fife is the broad, fertile valley of the River Eden. The A91 runs through its villages, including Gateside and Strathmiglo, with their red sandstone cottages, on the way east to St Andrews.

name: Road into St Andrews
description: The A91 crosses the Eden Estuary at Guardbridge and runs along the edge of the links into St Andrews.

name: St Andrews
description: St Andrews is a small coastal town known for Scotland's oldest university, founded in 1413, and the ruins of St Andrews Cathedral, once the largest church in Scotland. St Salvator's Chapel and St Mary's College are part of the university.

name: The Old Course
description: The Old Course is often called the home of golf; it has been played for about 600 years. The Royal and Ancient clubhouse stands behind the first tee, and the Swilcan Bridge crosses the burn on the first and eighteenth holes. The course closes to golf on Sundays and becomes a public park.

name: Eden Course
description: The Eden Course, opened in 1914, is one of the seven public courses of St Andrews Links. It runs alongside the Eden Estuary, west of the Old Course.

name: Fairmont St Andrews
description: A clifftop resort a few kilometres southeast of St Andrews, with two golf courses, the Torrance and the Kittocks, looking out over St Andrews Bay. The Fairmont was our homebase for several days before moving into a flat in town for our last few days in St Andrews.

name: The Castle Course
description: The Castle Course, opened in 2008, is the newest course of St Andrews Links. It runs along the cliffs east of town, with views back over St Andrews Bay. It was so foggy that day; we couldn't see a thing for the first 16 holes. Caddies dropped markers in front of us to show us where to hit it, and Rita and I simply played a match rather than keeping score. The gloom rolled away just in time for us to see the beautiful 17th as we played it.

name: Kingsbarns Golf Links
description: Kingsbarns Golf Links opened in 2000 on the coast near the village of Kingsbarns, about 10 km southeast of St Andrews. Every hole has a view of the sea.

name: Dumbarnie Links
description: Dumbarnie Links opened in 2020 on the shore of Largo Bay, between Lower Largo and Elie, on Fife's south coast.

name: Royal Mile and Victoria Street
description: The Royal Mile runs down the spine of Edinburgh's Old Town from the castle to Holyrood. St Giles' Cathedral stands on it, and Victoria Street, with its curve of brightly painted shopfronts, drops from it toward the Grassmarket.

name: Princes Street Gardens
description: The gardens fill the valley between the Old Town and the New Town, below Edinburgh Castle. The Scott Monument, a Gothic spire built in memory of Sir Walter Scott, stands at the east end, and the Ross Bandstand in the west gardens hosts concerts.

name: Lauriston Place
description: Lauriston Place, on the southern edge of the Old Town, is lined with Victorian Scottish baronial buildings, including the former Royal Infirmary, now the Quartermile development.

name: Usher Hall and the West End
description: The Usher Hall, a domed concert hall that opened in 1914, stands on Lothian Road in Edinburgh's West End, below the castle rock.

name: Holyrood Park
description: A royal park on the east side of Edinburgh, around the cliffs of Salisbury Crags and the extinct volcano of Arthur's Seat.

name: New Town
description: Edinburgh's Georgian New Town, laid out from the 1760s, is a grid of wide streets and stone terraces north of Princes Street.
